Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 76, verses 1–6:

Meccan, and it contains one thousand four hundred and fifty letters, two hundred and forty words, and thirty-one verses.

Nafil ibn Raqim informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Shadhah related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Muslim ibn Qutaybah related to us from Shu'bah, from 'Asim, from Zirr, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites the surah Hal Ata, his reward from Allah will be Paradise and silk." [76] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/206.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Has there come upon man a period of time when he was not a thing worth mentioning?﴾ "Man" (al-insan) here refers to Adam (peace be upon him), who was the first to be named by this name. "A period of time" means forty years, during which he lay, thrown between Makkah and al-Ta'if, before the spirit was breathed into him. "He was not a thing worth mentioning" means he was not mentioned, not known, and did not know what his name was or what was intended by it. It is narrated that 'Umar heard a man recite: "Has there come upon man a period of time when he was not a thing worth mentioning?" and 'Umar said: "I wish it had been completed [and not come to pass]." 'Awn ibn 'Abd Allah said: A man recited this verse in the presence of Ibn Mas'ud, and he said: "Only, I wish that were so."

﴿Indeed, We created man﴾ meaning the children of Adam, ﴿from a drop of mixed fluid﴾ meaning from the semen of the man and the semen of the woman. Every small quantity of water in a container is a "nutfah" (drop), as in the saying of 'Abd Allah ibn Rawahah: "You are nothing but a drop." Its plural is nutaf and nutf, and its root is from "natafa," meaning it dripped. ﴿Amshaj﴾ means mixtures; its singular is "mashj" or "mashij," like "hadhan" and "hadhin." Ru'bah said:

"They throw down every hastening weaver... who has not clothed a skin in mixed blood."

It is said: "Mashajtu hadha bihadha," meaning I mixed this with that, so it is "mamshuj" and "mashj," like "makhlut" and "khalit." Abu Dawad said:

"As if the feathers and what is above them of it, opposite the blade, its two sides are a mixture."

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan, 'Ikrimah, Mujahid and al-Rabi' said: it means the fluid of the man and the fluid of the woman mix in the womb, and the child is formed from both of them together. The fluid of the man is white and thick, and the fluid of the woman is yellow and thin; whichever of them overcomes the other, the resemblance is to it. Qatadah said: they are the stages of creation: a drop, then a clot, then a lump of flesh, then bones, then He clothes the bones with flesh, then He produces it as another creation.

Al-Dahhak said: it means the varying colours of the drop: the man's drop is white and red, and the woman's drop is green and red, so it is of varying colours. This is the narration of al-Wali from Ibn 'Abbas, and Ibn Abi Najih from Mujahid. Likewise 'Ata' al-Khurasani and al-Kalbi said: the "amshaj" are redness within whiteness and whiteness within redness, or yellowness.

'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud and Usamah ibn Zayd said: they are the veins that are in the drop. Ibn Jurayj narrated from 'Ata', who said: the "amshaj" are the "hin" that is like a clot. Al-Hasan said: Yes, by Allah, you were created from a drop mixed with blood, which is the blood of menstruation; when she conceives, the menstruation is lifted. Yaman said: any two colours that mix are "amshaj." Ibn al-Sikkit said: "al-amshaj" are mixtures, because it is combined from various kinds, so man was created with differing natures. The scholars of meanings (Ahl al-Ma'ani) said: the form "amshaj" is a plural pattern but has the sense of the singular, because it describes "nutfah"; this is like saying "barmah a'shar" (a pot with pieces) and "thawb akhlaq" (a worn garment) and similar.

I heard Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami say: I heard Abu 'Uthman al-Maghribi say: I was asked while I was in Makkah about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿amshaj, We test him﴾, and I said: Allah tested creation with nine mixtures: three that are tempting, three that are disbelieving, and three that are believing. As for the three tempting ones, they are his hearing, his sight and his tongue; as for the three disbelieving ones, they are his self (nafs), his desire (hawa) and his devil (shaytan); as for the three believing ones, they are his intellect ('aql), his spirit (ruh) and his sovereign (malik). So when Allah supports the servant with aid, the intellect settles over the heart and rules it, the self and desire are taken captive and find no way to move, the spirit becomes akin to the self, the intellect becomes akin to desire, and the Word of Allah becomes the highest: ﴿And fight them until there is no more fitnah﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 193].

﴿We test him﴾, We examine him through command and prohibition. Some grammarians of Arabic said: it is a preposed clause whose meaning is delayed, its sense being: ﴿So We made him hearing and seeing﴾, because the test does not occur except after the completion of the creation. ﴿Indeed, We guided him to the way﴾, meaning We made clear to him the way of truth and falsehood, guidance and misguidance, and We made him know the path of good and evil; this is like His saying: ﴿And We guided him to the two highways﴾ [Surah al-Balad: 10]. ﴿Either grateful or ungrateful﴾: either a believer, fortunate, or a disbeliever, wretched; meaning, We created him to be either this or that. It was also said that the meaning of the statement is recompense, meaning: We made the way clear to him, whether he is thankful or ungrateful; this is the choice of al-Farra'. Then He distinguished the two groups, so the Mighty One said: ﴿Indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers chains, and shackles, and a blazing fire.﴾ Each chain is seventy cubits long.

﴿And shackles and a blazing fire﴾. Abu Ja'far, Shaybah, Nafi', 'Asim through Hafs, al-A'mash, al-Kisa'i and Ayyub all recited "salasila" with the alif present in pause and with tanwin in continuity; this is the choice of Abu 'Ubayd, and it is the narration of Hisham from the people of Syria. Its opposite is recited by Hamzah, Khalaf, [Qunbul], Ya'qub through the narration of [....] [[Blank space in the manuscript.]] and Zayd. Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr recited "qawarira" (the first) with an alif and the second without an alif.

Abu 'Ubayd said: I saw in the Imam 'Uthman's copy of the Qur'an the first "qawarira" written with an alif, and the second had an alif which was erased, and I saw its trace clearly there. [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi in detail: 19/123.]]

﴿Indeed, the righteous﴾ meaning the believers who are sincere in their faith and obedient to their Lord. Al-Hasan said: they are those who do not harm an atom and do not cause evil. Their singular is "barr," like "shahid" and "ashhad," "nasir" and "ansar," "sahib" and "ashab"; it is used in the sense of "nahr" and "anhar," and "darb" and "adrab."

﴿They will drink﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿from a cup whose mixture is of camphor﴾. Qatadah said: it is mixed for them with camphor and sealed for them with musk. 'Ikrimah said: its "mizaj" is its taste. The scholars of meanings said: He means like camphor in its whiteness, the fragrance of its scent and its coolness, because camphor is not drunk; this is like His saying: ﴿until, when he made it a fire﴾ [Surah al-Kahf: 96], meaning like fire. Ibn Kaysan said: it was perfumed with camphor, musk and ginger. Al-Farra' said: it is said that camphor is the name of a spring of water in Paradise. In the codex of 'Abd Allah it reads: "from a cup, yellow, whose mixture was qafur," and the qaf and kaf interchange, as they are both uvular sounds. Al-Wasiti said: when their states differed in the world, their drinks differed in the Hereafter; the cup of camphor cooled what was burning in their breasts in this world.

﴿A spring﴾ is in the accusative because it follows "camphor" as an explanation of it. Al-Kisa'i said: it is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal) and as a detached word (qat'). It was said: "They drink a spring," and it was said: "from a spring," and it was said: "I mean a spring," and it was said: it is in the accusative of praise; all these possibilities are admissible.

﴿A spring from which the servants of Allah drink; they cause it to gush forth in abundance.﴾ The "ba'" in "yashrabu biha" means the drinking of it, and the "ba'" is extra; it was also said it means "minha" (from it). ﴿Yufajjiruna haa taf'jira﴾ means they lead it wherever they wish, from their dwellings and palaces, just as one of you makes a river flow in this world here and there to wherever he wants.

Abu 'Ubayd said: I saw in the Imam 'Uthman's copy of the Qur'an the first "qawarira" written with an alif, and the second had an alif which was erased, and I saw its trace clearly there. [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi in detail: 19/123.]]

﴿Indeed, the righteous﴾ meaning the believers who are sincere in their faith and obedient to their Lord. Al-Hasan said: they are those who do not harm an atom and do not cause evil. ﴿They will drink﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿from a cup whose mixture is of camphor﴾. Qatadah said: it is mixed for them with camphor and sealed for them with musk. 'Ikrimah said: its "mizaj" is its taste. Al-Wasiti said: when their states differed in the world, their drinks differed in the Hereafter; the cup of camphor cooled what was burning in their breasts in this world.

It was said: "They drink a spring," and it was said: "from a spring," and it was said: "I mean a spring," and it was said: it is in the accusative of praise; all these possibilities are admissible.

﴿They fulfil their vows﴾. Qatadah said: by what God, exalted is He, made obligatory upon them, such as prayer, zakat, hajj, umrah and other duties. Mujahid and ‘Ikrimah said: it means that when they vowed to obey God, they fulfilled it.
