"She departed, and she had left in the heart a crack
spreading far, despite her distance."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/128.]]

﴿And they give food, despite their love for it﴾. Ibn ‘Abbas said: despite its scarcity, their own need for it, and their desire for it. Al-Dari said: out of love for God. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: out of love for giving food.
﴿to the needy, the orphan and the captive﴾. The captive is the non-Muslim enemy seized by force, or the Muslim imprisoned with just cause. Qatadah said: after God commanded that captives be treated well, their captives at that time were from the polytheists, so your Muslim brother is more deserving that you feed him.
Mujahid, Sa‘id ibn Jubayr and ‘Ata said: it is the imprisoned person from among the People of the Qibla (Muslims).

Al-Hasan informed me, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Najiyah narrated to us, saying: ‘Abbad ibn Ahmad al-‘Arzami narrated to us, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to us, from his father, from ‘Amr ibn Qays, from ‘Atiyyah, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding ﴿And they give food, despite their love for it, to the needy﴾, that he said: "the poor"; ﴿and the orphan﴾, he said: "one who has no father"; ﴿and the captive﴾, he said: "the slave and the imprisoned."

Abu Hamzah al-Thumali said: the captive is the woman. The evidence for this interpretation is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Treat women well, for they are with you as captives." [[Sunan Ibn Majah: 1/594.]]

﴿We feed you only for the sake of God. We do not desire from you any reward or thanks.﴾ In it there are two readings: first, that shukūr is the plural of shukr, like fulūs as the plural of fals and kufūr as the plural of kufr; second, that it is a verbal noun, like fu‘ūl, dukhūl and khurūj.

Mujahid and Sa‘id ibn Jubayr said: they did not say this aloud, but God knew it from their hearts, so He praised them so that whoever desires it may be encouraged.

﴿Indeed, we fear from our Lord a Day that is frowning﴾, in which faces will frown because of its severity and abundance of hardships. He attributed the frowning to the Day, as one says "a fasting day" and "a sleeping night." Ibn ‘Abbas said: the disbeliever will frown on that day until sweat like tar flows from between his eyes. It was also said: the Day was described as frowning because of its hardship and terror, like a man with a grim and wretched face.

﴿Long and harsh﴾. ‘Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: "al-‘abus" means constriction, and "al-qamṭarīr" means long. Al-Kalbi said: "al-‘abus" is that which has no expansiveness, and "al-qamṭarīr" is severe. Qatadah, Mujahid and Muqatil said: "al-qamṭarīr" is that which contracts the faces, seizes life, and makes the space between the eyes contract because of its severity. Al-Akhfash said: al-qamṭarīr is the most intense and longest of days in affliction; it is said: yawm qamṭarīr and qamāṭir, when it is severe in its hardship. The poet said:
"They fled when the war's dust rose,
and the frowning, harsh day pressed upon them."
Al-Farra’ recited:
"Sons of our paternal uncle, do you remember our suffering
against you, when there was a harsh day?"
[[Al-Sihah: 2/797.]]
Al-Kisa’i said: iqmaṭarra al-qawm and izmaharra, iqmiṭrāran and izmihrāran, and it is zamharir and qamṭarir. A day is "muqmaṭir" when it is difficult and severe. Al-Hudhali said:
"The sons of war nursed us for them, a harsh milk,
so whoever of us meets that day flees."
[[The same source. In Taj al-‘Arus (3/507) it is narrated: "with it a harsh milk; whoever meets it meets a trained chief."]]

﴿So God protected them from the evil of that Day which they feared, and gave them radiance in their faces and joy in their hearts, and rewarded them for what they endured patiently﴾, in obedience to God and in abstaining from His disobedience. Al-Dahhak said: for poverty. Al-Qurtubi said: for fasting. ‘Ata said: for hunger.

Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab narrated from ‘Umar, who said: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was asked about patience, and he said: "Patience is of four kinds: first, patience at the first shock; second, patience in performing the obligations; third, patience in avoiding what God has forbidden; and fourth, patience in calamities." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/136.]]

﴿A garden and silk﴾. Al-Hasan said: He will admit them to Paradise and clothe them in silk.
﴿Reclining therein upon couches﴾, accusative as a circumstantial clause. ﴿Therein﴾, in Paradise. ﴿Upon couches﴾, the thrones inside canopied chambers; an arika is not called such unless both conditions are met. Al-Hasan said: this is the dialect of the people of Yemen, where a great man among them would make an arika, and it would be said: "the arika of so-and-so."

Muqatil said: al-ara’ik are thrones within canopied chambers, of pearls and rubies, interwoven with bars of gold and silver and various kinds of jewels.

﴿They will see therein neither sun nor bitter cold﴾, i.e. neither scorching heat nor freezing cold.
Qatadah said: God, exalted is He, knew that intense heat harms and intense cold harms, so God protected them from both harms together. Murrah al-Hamdani said: al-zamharir is the piercing cold. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: it is something like the heads of needles that descends from the sky in extreme cold. Ibn Mas‘ud said: it is a kind of punishment, which is intense cold.

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn ‘Imran al-Sawadi say: I heard Abu al-‘Abbas Ahmad ibn Yahya Tha‘lab, when he was asked about God's saying ﴿They will see therein neither sun nor bitter cold﴾, say: al-zamharir is the moon in the dialect of Tayy. Their poet said:
"A night whose darkness was thick,
I crossed it while the zamharir shone."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/138.]]
That is, the moon had not risen.

The scholars differed concerning the occasion of revelation of these verses. Muqatil said: they were revealed concerning a man from the Ansar who fed a needy person, an orphan and a captive in one day, and this was his story.

Ibn Fatjuwayh informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalaf ibn Hayyan narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn ‘Isa narrated to us, saying: ‘Ali ibn ‘Ali ibn Abi Hamzah al-Thumali narrated to us, saying: It reached us that a needy man came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, feed me." He said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, I have nothing with which to feed you, but I will seek." So he came to a man from the Ansar who was having his evening meal with his wife, and said to him: "I came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and asked him to feed me, and he said: 'I have nothing to feed you, but I will seek.'" The Ansari said to his wife: "What do you think?" She said: "Feed him and give him to drink." Then an orphan came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, feed me." He said: "I have nothing to feed you, but I will seek." So the orphan came to the Ansari who had been visited by the needy man and said: "Feed me." He said to his wife: "What do you think?" She said: "Feed him." So he fed him. Then a captive came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, feed me." He said: "By God, I have nothing to feed you, but I will seek." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/130.]] So the captive came to the Ansari and said: "Feed me." He said to his wife: "What do you think?" She said: "Feed him." All of this happened in a single hour, so God, exalted is He, revealed concerning what the Ansari did in feeding the needy, the orphan and the captive: ﴿And they give food, despite their love for it, to the needy, the orphan and the captive﴾.

Others said: they were revealed concerning ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib, Fatimah, and their servant girl called Fiddah, and the story is as follows.

Al-Shaykh Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Ali al-Shaybani al-‘Adl informed us, reading it to him in Safar of the year three hundred and eighty-seven, saying: Ibn al-Sharqi informed us, saying: Mahbub ibn Hamid al-Nasri narrated to us, saying: Abu Muhammad ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Wahhab al-Khawwar, cousin of al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, narrated to us in the year two hundred and fifty-eight, and Rawh ibn ‘Ubadah asked him about this hadith, saying: al-Qayyim ibn Mihram narrated to us from Layth, from Mujahid, from Ibn ‘Abbas. And ‘Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Abu Muhammad Ahmad ibn ‘Abd Allah al-Muzani informed us, saying: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Suhayl ibn ‘Ali ibn Mihran al-Bahili narrated to us in Basra, saying: Abu Mas‘ud ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Fahd ibn Hilal narrated to us, saying: al-Ghanim ibn Yahya narrated to us, from Abu ‘Ali al-Qayri, from Muhammad ibn al-Sa’ir, from Abu Salih, from Ibn ‘Abbas. Abu al-Hasan ibn Mihran said: and Muhammad ibn Zakariyya al-Basri narrated to me, saying: Sa‘id ibn Waqid al-Muzani narrated to me, saying: al-Qasim ibn Bahram narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, from Ibn ‘Abbas, concerning God's saying ﴿They fulfil their vows, and fear a Day whose evil will be widespread﴾, that he said: al-Hasan and al-Husayn fell ill, and their grandfather Muhammad, the Messenger of God (ﷺ), visited them, with Abu Bakr and ‘Umar (may God be pleased with them both). The common Arabs also visited them, and they said: "O Abu al-Hasan, if you would vow a vow for your two sons. Every vow that is not fulfilled is nothing."

‘Ali (may God be pleased with him) said: "If my two sons recover from what they have, I will fast three days in thanks." Fatimah (may God be pleased with her) said: "If my two sons recover from what they have, I will fast three days for God in thanks." The two boys had not worn health, and there was nothing, little or much, with the family of Muhammad. So ‘Ali (may God be pleased with him) went to Shim‘un ibn Jaba al-Khaybari, who was a Jew, and borrowed from him three sa‘ of barley. In the narration of al-Muzani from Ibn Mihran al-Bahili: he went to a Jewish neighbour of his who worked wool, called Shim‘un ibn Jaba, and said: "Would you give me a fleece of wool, which the daughter of Muhammad (ﷺ) will spin for you in exchange for three sa‘ of barley?" He said: "Yes." So he gave it to him, and he brought the wool and the barley and informed Fatimah of this, and she accepted and obeyed.

They said: Fatimah (may God be pleased with her) stood up to one sa‘, ground it, and baked from it five loaves, one loaf for each of them. ‘Ali prayed the maghrib with the Prophet (ﷺ), then came to the house and placed the food before them. Suddenly a needy man came and stood at the door and said: "Peace be upon you, people of the house of Muhammad. A needy man from the needy Muslims: feed me, and God will feed you from the tables of Paradise." ‘Ali (may God be pleased with him) heard him and began to say:
"Fatimah, possessor of glory and certainty,
daughter of the best of all people,
do you not see the wretched needy man
who has stood at the door, moaning for him?
He complains to God and submits,
he complains to us, a hungry, sorrowful one.
Every person is held in pledge by his deeds,
and the doer of good will be made manifest.
Our promise is the garden of ‘Illiyyin,
which God has forbidden to the miser.
For the miser there is a humiliating station:
the fire will hurl him down into the prison.
His drink is boiling water and pus,
whoever does good will be made fat,
and will enter Paradise at any time."
Then Fatimah said:
"Your command is obeyed by me, cousin,
there is no baseness in me nor lowliness.
I was nourished on bread that has its craft,
I will feed him and not care for the hour.
I hope, when I satisfy the hungry one,
to join the righteous and the community,
and enter the eternal garden, and I have intercession."
He said: So they gave him the food, and they remained their day and night without tasting anything but plain water. When the second day came, Fatimah stood to another sa‘, ground it and baked it, and ‘Ali prayed with the Prophet (ﷺ). Then he came to the house and placed the food before them. Suddenly an orphan came and stood at the door and said: "Peace be upon you, people of the house of Muhammad. An orphan from the children of the emigrants; my father was martyred on the day of ‘Aqabah. Feed me, and God will feed you on the tables of Paradise." ‘Ali (may God be pleased with him) heard him and began to say:
"Fatimah, daughter of the noble master,
daughter of a prophet, not of the ignoble,
God has brought the orphan,
whoever shows mercy today will be shown mercy.
His promise is in the garden of bliss,
the eternity has been forbidden to the base.
Is it not that he will cross the straight path?
He who slips will fall into the fire of Hell."
Then Fatimah said:
"I feed him today and do not care,
and I prefer God over my children.
They have become hungry, and they are my cubs,
the youngest of them will be killed in battle.
At Karbala he will be killed by treachery,
for the killer there is woe and calamity.
Into the fire he will be hurled to the lowest depths,
and in his hands are fetters and chains,
his shackles increased over the shackles."
He said: So they gave him the food, and they remained two days and two nights without tasting anything but plain water. When it was the third day, Fatimah (may God be pleased with her) stood to the remaining sa‘, ground it and baked it, and ‘Ali prayed with the Prophet (ﷺ). Then he came to the house and placed the food before them. Suddenly a captive came and stood at the door and said: "Peace be upon you, people of the house of Muhammad. You take us captive [and bind us] and do not feed us. Feed me, for I am a captive of Muhammad. God will feed you on the tables of Paradise." ‘Ali heard him and began to say:
"Fatimah, daughter of the Prophet Ahmad,
daughter of a prophet, lord of the honoured,
this is a captive of the guided Prophet,
bound and shackled in his fetter,
he complains to us of hunger, it has stretched out.
Whoever feeds today will find it from tomorrow.
With the exalted, the one, the unifier,
what the sower sows, he will reap."
Then Fatimah said:
"Nothing remained of what had come except one sa‘.
My hand has gone with the forearm.
My sons, by God, are hungry.
O Lord, do not leave them lost.
Their father is one of good works,
who does kindness by innovation,
broad of forearms, long of reach,
and on my head is no veil,
except a veil woven of thongs."
He said: So they gave him the food, and they remained three days and nights without tasting anything but plain water. When it was the fourth day, and they had fulfilled their vow, ‘Ali (may God be pleased with him) took al-Hasan with his right hand and al-Husayn with his left, and came toward the Messenger of God (ﷺ), while they were trembling like chicks from the intensity of hunger. When the Prophet (ﷺ) saw them, he said: "O Abu al-Hasan, how grievous it is to me to see you in this state. Go to my daughter Fatimah." So they went to her, and she was in her prayer niche, her belly stuck to her back from intense hunger, and her eyes were sunken. When the Prophet (ﷺ) saw her, he said: "Woe, O God's help! The people of the house of Muhammad are dying of hunger." Then Gabriel (peace be upon him) descended and said: "O Muhammad, take it; God has blessed you in your household." He said: "What have we taken, O Gabriel?" [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/134; and Manaqib al-Khwarazmi: 270.]] Then he recited ﴿Has there come upon man a period of time﴾ up to his saying ﴿and not thanks﴾, to the end of the surah.

Qatadah ibn Mihran al-Bahili said in this hadith: The Prophet (ﷺ) leapt up until he entered upon Fatimah, and when he saw their state he bent over them weeping. Then he said: "You have been in this state for three days, as I see, and I was unaware of you." Then Gabriel (peace be upon him) descended with these verses: ﴿Indeed the righteous will drink from a cup whose mixture is camphor, a spring from which the servants of God will drink, making it gush forth in abundance.﴾ He said: it is a spring in the house of the Prophet (ﷺ) that gushes forth to the houses of the prophets (peace be upon them) and the believers.

﴿They fulfil their vows﴾, meaning ‘Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan, al-Husayn and their servant girl Fiddah. ﴿And they fear a Day whose evil will be widespread﴾. ﴿And they give food, despite their love for it﴾, meaning despite their desire for food, and preferring a needy person from the needy Muslims, an orphan from the orphans of the Muslims, and a captive from the captives of the polytheists. And when they fed them, they would say: ﴿We feed you only for the sake of God. We do not desire from you any reward or thanks. Indeed, we fear from our Lord a frowning Day, harsh﴾. He said: By God, they did not say this with their tongues, but they concealed it in their souls, so God, exalted is He, informed of their concealment: they say, ﴿We do not desire from you any reward or thanks﴾, so that they would not impose upon us by it, but we gave you for the sake of God and seeking His reward. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿So God protected them from the evil of that Day, and gave them radiance in their faces and joy in their hearts, and rewarded them for what they endured patiently: a garden in which to dwell, and silk to wear and to spread beneath them, reclining therein upon couches, they will see therein neither sun nor bitter cold.﴾

Ibn ‘Abbas said: While the people of Paradise are in Paradise, they will see a light like the light of the sun, and the gardens will shine with it. The people of Paradise will say: "O Ridwan!" He said: our Lord, mighty and majestic, says ﴿They will see therein neither sun nor bitter cold﴾. Ridwan will say to them: "This is neither sun nor moon, but this is Fatimah and ‘Ali laughing, laughing, and the gardens shine with the light of their laughter." And concerning them God, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿Has there come upon man a period of time﴾ to His saying: ﴿and your effort has been thankfully accepted.﴾

And I recited concerning him:
"I am the client of a young man
concerning whom ‘Has there come upon man' was revealed."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/138.]]

In light of this view, the surah is Madani. The scholars differed about when this surah was revealed. Mujahid and Qatadah said: all of it is Madani. Al-Hasan and Ikrimah said: one verse of it is Makki, namely His words, glory be to Him, ﴿So do not obey from among them any sinner or ungrateful one﴾, and the rest is Madani. Others said: all of it is Makki. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 76, verses 7–13 (part 1 of 2):

﴿They fulfil their vows﴾. Qatadah said: by what God, exalted is He, made obligatory upon them, such as prayer, zakat, hajj, umrah and other duties. Mujahid and ‘Ikrimah said: it means that when they vowed to obey God, they fulfilled it.

﴿And they fear a Day whose evil will be widespread﴾, i.e. extended and harsh. It is said: istatara al-sad'u fi al-zujajah (the crack spread through the glass) and istaṭāla, when it extended. From this is the saying of al-A‘sha:
"She departed, and she had left in the heart a crack
spreading far, despite her distance."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/128.]]

﴿And they give food, despite their love for it﴾. Ibn ‘Abbas said: despite its scarcity, their own need for it, and their desire for it. Al-Dari said: out of love for God. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: out of love for giving food.
﴿to the needy, the orphan and the captive﴾. The captive is the non-Muslim enemy seized by force, or the Muslim imprisoned with just cause. Qatadah said: after God commanded that captives be treated well, their captives at that time were from the polytheists, so your Muslim brother is more deserving that you feed him.
Mujahid, Sa‘id ibn Jubayr and ‘Ata said: it is the imprisoned person from among the People of the Qibla (Muslims).

Al-Hasan informed me, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Najiyah narrated to us, saying: ‘Abbad ibn Ahmad al-‘Arzami narrated to us, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to us, from his father, from ‘Amr ibn Qays, from ‘Atiyyah, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding ﴿And they give food, despite their love for it, to the needy﴾, that he said: "the poor"; ﴿and the orphan﴾, he said: "one who has no father"; ﴿and the captive﴾, he said: "the slave and the imprisoned."

Abu Hamzah al-Thumali said: the captive is the woman. The evidence for this interpretation is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Treat women well, for they are with you as captives." [[Sunan Ibn Majah: 1/594.]]

﴿We feed you only for the sake of God. We do not desire from you any reward or thanks.﴾ In it there are two readings: first, that shukūr is the plural of shukr, like fulūs as the plural of fals and kufūr as the plural of kufr; second, that it is a verbal noun, like fu‘ūl, dukhūl and khurūj.

Mujahid and Sa‘id ibn Jubayr said: they did not say this aloud, but God knew it from their hearts, so He praised them so that whoever desires it may be encouraged.

﴿Indeed, we fear from our Lord a Day that is frowning﴾, in which faces will frown because of its severity and abundance of hardships. He attributed the frowning to the Day, as one says "a fasting day" and "a sleeping night." Ibn ‘Abbas said: the disbeliever will frown on that day until sweat like tar flows from between his eyes. It was also said: the Day was described as frowning because of its hardship and terror, like a man with a grim and wretched face.

﴿Long and harsh﴾. ‘Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: "al-‘abus" means constriction, and "al-qamṭarīr" means long. Al-Kalbi said: "al-‘abus" is that which has no expansiveness, and "al-qamṭarīr" is severe. Qatadah, Mujahid and Muqatil said: "al-qamṭarīr" is that which contracts the faces, seizes life, and makes the space between the eyes contract because of its severity. Al-Akhfash said: al-qamṭarīr is the most intense and longest of days in affliction; it is said: yawm qamṭarīr and qamāṭir, when it is severe in its hardship. The poet said:
"They fled when the war's dust rose,
and the frowning, harsh day pressed upon them."
Al-Farra’ recited:
"Sons of our paternal uncle, do you remember our suffering
against you, when there was a harsh day?"
[[Al-Sihah: 2/797.]]
Al-Kisa’i said: iqmaṭarra al-qawm and izmaharra, iqmiṭrāran and izmihrāran, and it is zamharir and qamṭarir. A day is "muqmaṭir" when it is difficult and severe. Al-Hudhali said:
"The sons of war nursed us for them, a harsh milk,
so whoever of us meets that day flees."
[[The same source. In Taj al-‘Arus (3/507) it is narrated: "with it a harsh milk; whoever meets it meets a trained chief."]]

﴿So God protected them from the evil of that Day which they feared, and gave them radiance in their faces and joy in their hearts, and rewarded them for what they endured patiently﴾, in obedience to God and in abstaining from His disobedience. Al-Dahhak said: for poverty. Al-Qurtubi said: for fasting. ‘Ata said: for hunger.

Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab narrated from ‘Umar, who said: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was asked about patience, and he said: "Patience is of four kinds: first, patience at the first shock; second, patience in performing the obligations; third, patience in avoiding what God has forbidden; and fourth, patience in calamities." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/136.]]

﴿A garden and silk﴾. Al-Hasan said: He will admit them to Paradise and clothe them in silk.
﴿Reclining therein upon couches﴾, accusative as a circumstantial clause. ﴿Therein﴾, in Paradise. ﴿Upon couches﴾, the thrones inside canopied chambers; an arika is not called such unless both conditions are met. Al-Hasan said: this is the dialect of the people of Yemen, where a great man among them would make an arika, and it would be said: "the arika of so-and-so."

Muqatil said: al-ara’ik are thrones within canopied chambers, of pearls and rubies, interwoven with bars of gold and silver and various kinds of jewels.

﴿They will see therein neither sun nor bitter cold﴾, i.e. neither scorching heat nor freezing cold.
Qatadah said: God, exalted is He, knew that intense heat harms and intense cold harms, so God protected them from both harms together. Murrah al-Hamdani said: al-zamharir is the piercing cold. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: it is something like the heads of needles that descends from the sky in extreme cold. Ibn Mas‘ud said: it is a kind of punishment, which is intense cold.

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn ‘Imran al-Sawadi say: I heard Abu al-‘Abbas Ahmad ibn Yahya Tha‘lab, when he was asked about God's saying ﴿They will see therein neither sun nor bitter cold﴾, say: al-zamharir is the moon in the dialect of Tayy. Their poet said:
"A night whose darkness was thick,
I crossed it while the zamharir shone."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/138.]]
That is, the moon had not risen.

The scholars differed concerning the occasion of revelation of these verses. Muqatil said: they were revealed concerning a man from the Ansar who fed a needy person, an orphan and a captive in one day, and this was his story.

Ibn Fatjuwayh informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalaf ibn Hayyan narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn ‘Isa narrated to us, saying: ‘Ali ibn ‘Ali ibn Abi Hamzah al-Thumali narrated to us, saying: It reached us that a needy man came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, feed me." He said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, I have nothing with which to feed you, but I will seek." So he came to a man from the Ansar who was having his evening meal with his wife, and said to him: "I came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and asked him to feed me, and he said: 'I have nothing to feed you, but I will seek.'" The Ansari said to his wife: "What do you think?" She said: "Feed him and give him to drink." Then an orphan came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, feed me." He said: "I have nothing to feed you, but I will seek." So the orphan came to the Ansari who had been visited by the needy man and said: "Feed me." He said to his wife: "What do you think?" She said: "Feed him." So he fed him. Then a captive came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, feed me." He said: "By God, I have nothing to feed you, but I will seek." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/130.]] So the captive came to the Ansari and said: "Feed me." He said to his wife: "What do you think?" She said: "Feed him." All of this happened in a single hour, so God, exalted is He, revealed concerning what the Ansari did in feeding the needy, the orphan and the captive: ﴿And they give food, despite their love for it, to the needy, the orphan and the captive﴾.

Others said: they were revealed concerning ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib, Fatimah, and their servant girl called Fiddah, and the story is as follows.

Al-Shaykh Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Ali al-Shaybani al-‘Adl informed us, reading it to him in Safar of the year three hundred and eighty-seven, saying: Ibn al-Sharqi informed us, saying: Mahbub ibn Hamid al-Nasri narrated to us, saying: Abu Muhammad ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Wahhab al-Khawwar, cousin of al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, narrated to us in the year two hundred and fifty-eight, and Rawh ibn ‘Ubadah asked him about this hadith, saying: al-Qayyim ibn Mihram narrated to us from Layth, from Mujahid, from Ibn ‘Abbas. And ‘Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Abu Muhammad Ahmad ibn ‘Abd Allah al-Muzani informed us, saying: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Suhayl ibn ‘Ali ibn Mihran al-Bahili narrated to us in Basra, saying: Abu Mas‘ud ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Fahd ibn Hilal narrated to us, saying: al-Ghanim ibn Yahya narrated to us, from Abu ‘Ali al-Qayri, from Muhammad ibn al-Sa’ir, from Abu Salih, from Ibn ‘Abbas. Abu al-Hasan ibn Mihran said: and Muhammad ibn Zakariyya al-Basri narrated to me, saying: Sa‘id ibn Waqid al-Muzani narrated to me, saying: al-Qasim ibn Bahram narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, from Ibn ‘Abbas, concerning God's saying ﴿They fulfil their vows, and fear a Day whose evil will be widespread﴾, that he said: al-Hasan and al-Husayn fell ill, and their grandfather Muhammad, the Messenger of God (ﷺ), visited them, with Abu Bakr and ‘Umar (may God be pleased with them both). The common Arabs also visited them, and they said: "O Abu al-Hasan, if you would vow a vow for your two sons. Every vow that is not fulfilled is nothing."

‘Ali (may God be pleased with him) said: "If my two sons recover from what they have, I will fast three days in thanks." Fatimah (may God be pleased with her) said: "If my two sons recover from what they have, I will fast three days for God in thanks." The two boys had not worn health, and there was nothing, little or much, with the family of Muhammad. So ‘Ali (may God be pleased with him) went to Shim‘un ibn Jaba al-Khaybari, who was a Jew, and borrowed from him three sa‘ of barley. In the narration of al-Muzani from Ibn Mihran al-Bahili: he went to a Jewish neighbour of his who worked wool, called Shim‘un ibn Jaba, and said: "Would you give me a fleece of wool, which the daughter of Muhammad (ﷺ) will spin for you in exchange for three sa‘ of barley?" He said: "Yes." So he gave it to him, and he brought the wool and the barley and informed Fatimah of this, and she accepted and obeyed.

They said: Fatimah (may God be pleased with her) stood up to one sa‘, ground it, and baked from it five loaves, one loaf for each of them. ‘Ali prayed the maghrib with the Prophet (ﷺ), then came to the house and placed the food before them. Suddenly a needy man came and stood at the door and said: "Peace be upon you, people of the house of Muhammad. A needy man from the needy Muslims: feed me, and God will feed you from the tables of Paradise." ‘Ali (may God be pleased with him) heard him and began to say:
"Fatimah, possessor of glory and certainty,
daughter of the best of all people,
do you not see the wretched needy man
who has stood at the door, moaning for him?
He complains to God and submits,
he complains to us, a hungry, sorrowful one.
Every person is held in pledge by his deeds,
and the doer of good will be made manifest.
Our promise is the garden of ‘Illiyyin,
which God has forbidden to the miser.
For the miser there is a humiliating station:
the fire will hurl him down into the prison.
His drink is boiling water and pus,
whoever does good will be made fat,
and will enter Paradise at any time."
Then Fatimah said:
"Your command is obeyed by me, cousin,
there is no baseness in me nor lowliness.
I was nourished on bread that has its craft,
I will feed him and not care for the hour.
I hope, when I satisfy the hungry one,
to join the righteous and the community,
and enter the eternal garden, and I have intercession."
He said: So they gave him the food, and they remained their day and night without tasting anything but plain water. When the second day came, Fatimah stood to another sa‘, ground it and baked it, and ‘Ali prayed with the Prophet (ﷺ). Then he came to the house and placed the food before them. Suddenly an orphan came and stood at the door and said: "Peace be upon you, people of the house of Muhammad. An orphan from the children of the emigrants; my father was martyred on the day of ‘Aqabah. Feed me, and God will feed you on the tables of Paradise." ‘Ali (may God be pleased with him) heard him and began to say:
"Fatimah, daughter of the noble master,
daughter of a prophet, not of the ignoble,
God has brought the orphan,
whoever shows mercy today will be shown mercy.
His promise is in the garden of bliss,
the eternity has been forbidden to the base.
Is it not that he will cross the straight path?
He who slips will fall into the fire of Hell."
Then Fatimah said:
"I feed him today and do not care,
and I prefer God over my children.
They have become hungry, and they are my cubs,
the youngest of them will be killed in battle.
At Karbala he will be killed by treachery,
for the killer there is woe and calamity.
Into the fire he will be hurled to the lowest depths,
and in his hands are fetters and chains,
his shackles increased over the shackles."
He said: So they gave him the food, and they remained two days and two nights without tasting anything but plain water. When it was the third day, Fatimah (may God be pleased with her) stood to the remaining sa‘, ground it and baked it, and ‘Ali prayed with the Prophet (ﷺ). Then he came to the house and placed the food before them. Suddenly a captive came and stood at the door and said: "Peace be upon you, people of the house of Muhammad. You take us captive [and bind us] and do not feed us. Feed me, for I am a captive of Muhammad. God will feed you on the tables of Paradise." ‘Ali heard him and began to say:
"Fatimah, daughter of the Prophet Ahmad,
daughter of a prophet, lord of the honoured,
this is a captive of the guided Prophet,
bound and shackled in his fetter,
he complains to us of hunger, it has stretched out.
Whoever feeds today will find it from tomorrow.
With the exalted, the one, the unifier,
what the sower sows, he will reap."
Then Fatimah said:
"Nothing remained of what had come except one sa‘.
My hand has gone with the forearm.
My sons, by God, are hungry.
O Lord, do not leave them lost.
Their father is one of good works,
who does kindness by innovation,
broad of forearms, long of reach,
and on my head is no veil,
except a veil woven of thongs."
He said: So they gave him the food, and they remained three days and nights without tasting anything but plain water. When it was the fourth day, and they had fulfilled their vow, ‘Ali (may God be pleased with him) took al-Hasan with his right hand and al-Husayn with his left, and came toward the Messenger of God (ﷺ), while they were trembling like chicks from the intensity of hunger. When the Prophet (ﷺ) saw them, he said: "O Abu al-Hasan, how grievous it is to me to see you in this state. Go to my daughter Fatimah." So they went to her, and she was in her prayer niche, her belly stuck to her back from intense hunger, and her eyes were sunken. When the Prophet (ﷺ) saw her, he said: "Woe, O God's help! The people of the house of Muhammad are dying of hunger." Then Gabriel (peace be upon him) descended and said: "O Muhammad, take it; God has blessed you in your household." He said: "What have we taken, O Gabriel?" [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/134; and Manaqib al-Khwarazmi: 270.]] Then he recited ﴿Has there come upon man a period of time﴾ up to his saying ﴿and not thanks﴾, to the end of the surah.

Qatadah ibn Mihran al-Bahili said in this hadith: The Prophet (ﷺ) leapt up until he entered upon Fatimah, and when he saw their state he bent over them weeping. Then he said: "You have been in this state for three days, as I see, and I was unaware of you." Then Gabriel (peace be upon him) descended with these verses: ﴿Indeed the righteous will drink from a cup whose mixture is camphor, a spring from which the servants of God will drink, making it gush forth in abundance.﴾ He said: it is a spring in the house of the Prophet (ﷺ) that gushes forth to the houses of the prophets (peace be upon them) and the believers.

﴿They fulfil their vows﴾, meaning ‘Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan, al-Husayn and their servant girl Fiddah. ﴿And they fear a Day whose evil will be widespread﴾. ﴿And they give food, despite their love for it﴾, meaning despite their desire for food, and preferring a needy person from the needy Muslims, an orphan from the orphans of the Muslims, and a captive from the captives of the polytheists. And when they fed them, they would say: ﴿We feed you only for the sake of God. We do not desire from you any reward or thanks. Indeed, we fear from our Lord a frowning Day, harsh﴾. He said: By God, they did not say this with their tongues, but they concealed it in their souls, so God, exalted is He, informed of their concealment: they say, ﴿We do not desire from you any reward or thanks﴾, so that they would not impose upon us by it, but we gave you for the sake of God and seeking His reward. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿So God protected them from the evil of that Day, and gave them radiance in their faces and joy in their hearts, and rewarded them for what they endured patiently: a garden in which to dwell, and silk to wear and to spread beneath them, reclining therein upon couches, they will see therein neither sun nor bitter cold.﴾

Ibn ‘Abbas said: While the people of Paradise are in Paradise, they will see a light like the light of the sun, and the gardens will shine with it. The people of Paradise will say: "O Ridwan!" He said: our Lord, mighty and majestic, says ﴿They will see therein neither sun nor bitter cold﴾. Ridwan will say to them: "This is neither sun nor moon, but this is Fatimah and ‘Ali laughing, laughing, and the gardens shine with the light of their laughter." And concerning them God, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿Has there come upon man a period of time﴾ to His saying: ﴿and your effort has been thankfully accepted.﴾

And I recited concerning him:
"I am the client of a young man
concerning whom ‘Has there come upon man' was revealed."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/138.]]

In light of this view, the surah is Madani. The scholars differed about when this surah was revealed. Mujahid and Qatadah said: all of it is Madani. Al-Hasan and Ikrimah said: one verse of it is Makki, namely His words, glory be to Him, ﴿So do not obey from among them any sinner or ungrateful one﴾, and the rest is Madani. Others said: all of it is Makki. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 76, verses 7–13 (part 1 of 2):

﴿They fulfil their vows﴾. Qatadah said: by what God, exalted is He, made obligatory upon them, such as prayer, zakat, hajj, umrah and other duties. Mujahid and ‘Ikrimah said: it means that when they vowed to obey God, they fulfilled it.

﴿And they fear a Day whose evil will be widespread﴾, i.e. extended and harsh. It is said: istatara al-sad'u fi al-zujajah (the crack spread through the glass) and istaṭāla, when it extended. From this is the saying of al-A‘sha:
"She departed, and she had left in the heart a crack
spreading far, despite her distance."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/128.]]

﴿And they give food, despite their love for it﴾. Ibn ‘Abbas said: despite its scarcity, their own need for it, and their desire for it. Al-Dari said: out of love for God. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: out of love for giving food.
﴿to the needy, the orphan and the captive﴾. The captive is the non-Muslim enemy seized by force, or the Muslim imprisoned with just cause. Qatadah said: after God commanded that captives be treated well, their captives at that time were from the polytheists, so your Muslim brother is more deserving that you feed him.
Mujahid, Sa‘id ibn Jubayr and ‘Ata said: it is the imprisoned person from among the People of the Qibla (Muslims).

Al-Hasan informed me, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Najiyah narrated to us, saying: ‘Abbad ibn Ahmad al-‘Arzami narrated to us, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to us, from his father, from ‘Amr ibn Qays, from ‘Atiyyah, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding ﴿And they give food, despite their love for it, to the needy﴾, that he said: "the poor"; ﴿and the orphan﴾, he said: "one who has no father"; ﴿and the captive﴾, he said: "the slave and the imprisoned."

Abu Hamzah al-Thumali said: the captive is the woman. The evidence for this interpretation is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Treat women well, for they are with you as captives." [[Sunan Ibn Majah: 1/594.]]

﴿We feed you only for the sake of God. We do not desire from you any reward or thanks.﴾ In it there are two readings: first, that shukūr is the plural of shukr, like fulūs as the plural of fals and kufūr as the plural of kufr; second, that it is a verbal noun, like fu‘ūl, dukhūl and khurūj.

Mujahid and Sa‘id ibn Jubayr said: they did not say this aloud, but God knew it from their hearts, so He praised them so that whoever desires it may be encouraged.

﴿Indeed, we fear from our Lord a Day that is frowning﴾, in which faces will frown because of its severity and abundance of hardships. He attributed the frowning to the Day, as one says "a fasting day" and "a sleeping night." Ibn ‘Abbas said: the disbeliever will frown on that day until sweat like tar flows from between his eyes. It was also said: the Day was described as frowning because of its hardship and terror, like a man with a grim and wretched face.

﴿Long and harsh﴾. ‘Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: "al-‘abus" means constriction, and "al-qamṭarīr" means long. Al-Kalbi said: "al-‘abus" is that which has no expansiveness, and "al-qamṭarīr" is severe. Qatadah, Mujahid and Muqatil said: "al-qamṭarīr" is that which contracts the faces, seizes life, and makes the space between the eyes contract because of its severity. Al-Akhfash said: al-qamṭarīr is the most intense and longest of days in affliction; it is said: yawm qamṭarīr and qamāṭir, when it is severe in its hardship. The poet said:
"They fled when the war's dust rose,
and the frowning, harsh day pressed upon them."
Al-Farra’ recited:
"Sons of our paternal uncle, do you remember our suffering
against you, when there was a harsh day?"
[[Al-Sihah: 2/797.]]
Al-Kisa’i said: iqmaṭarra al-qawm and izmaharra, iqmiṭrāran and izmihrāran, and it is zamharir and qamṭarir. A day is "muqmaṭir" when it is difficult and severe. Al-Hudhali said:
"The sons of war nursed us for them, a harsh milk,
so whoever of us meets that day flees."
[[The same source. In Taj al-‘Arus (3/507) it is narrated: "with it a harsh milk; whoever meets it meets a trained chief."]]

﴿So God protected them from the evil of that Day which they feared, and gave them radiance in their faces and joy in their hearts, and rewarded them for what they endured patiently﴾, in obedience to God and in abstaining from His disobedience. Al-Dahhak said: for poverty. Al-Qurtubi said: for fasting. ‘Ata said: for hunger.

Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab narrated from ‘Umar, who said: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was asked about patience, and he said: "Patience is of four kinds: first, patience at the first shock; second, patience in performing the obligations; third, patience in avoiding what God has forbidden; and fourth, patience in calamities." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/136.]]

﴿A garden and silk﴾. Al-Hasan said: He will admit them to Paradise and clothe them in silk.
﴿Reclining therein upon couches﴾, accusative as a circumstantial clause. ﴿Therein﴾, in Paradise. ﴿Upon couches﴾, the thrones inside canopied chambers; an arika is not called such unless both conditions are met. Al-Hasan said: this is the dialect of the people of Yemen, where a great man among them would make an arika, and it would be said: "the arika of so-and-so."

Muqatil said: al-ara’ik are thrones within canopied chambers, of pearls and rubies, interwoven with bars of gold and silver and various kinds of jewels.

﴿They will see therein neither sun nor bitter cold﴾, i.e. neither scorching heat nor freezing cold.
Qatadah said: God, exalted is He, knew that intense heat harms and intense cold harms, so God protected them from both harms together. Murrah al-Hamdani said: al-zamharir is the piercing cold. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: it is something like the heads of needles that descends from the sky in extreme cold. Ibn Mas‘ud said: it is a kind of punishment, which is intense cold.

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn ‘Imran al-Sawadi say: I heard Abu al-‘Abbas Ahmad ibn Yahya Tha‘lab, when he was asked about God's saying ﴿They will see therein neither sun nor bitter cold﴾, say: al-zamharir is the moon in the dialect of Tayy. Their poet said:
"A night whose darkness was thick,
I crossed it while the zamharir shone."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/138.]]
That is, the moon had not risen.

The scholars differed concerning the occasion of revelation of these verses. Muqatil said: they were revealed concerning a man from the Ansar who fed a needy person, an orphan and a captive in one day, and this was his story.

Ibn Fatjuwayh informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalaf ibn Hayyan narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn ‘Isa narrated to us, saying: ‘Ali ibn ‘Ali ibn Abi Hamzah al-Thumali narrated to us, saying: It reached us that a needy man came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, feed me." He said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, I have nothing with which to feed you, but I will seek." So he came to a man from the Ansar who was having his evening meal with his wife, and said to him: "I came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and asked him to feed me, and he said: 'I have nothing to feed you, but I will seek.'" The Ansari said to his wife: "What do you think?" She said: "Feed him and give him to drink." Then an orphan came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, feed me." He said: "I have nothing to feed you, but I will seek." So the orphan came to the Ansari who had been visited by the needy man and said: "Feed me." He said to his wife: "What do you think?" She said: "Feed him." So he fed him. Then a captive came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, feed me." He said: "By God, I have nothing to feed you, but I will seek." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/130.]] So the captive came to the Ansari and said: "Feed me." He said to his wife: "What do you think?" She said: "Feed him." All of this happened in a single hour, so God, exalted is He, revealed concerning what the Ansari did in feeding the needy, the orphan and the captive: ﴿And they give food, despite their love for it, to the needy, the orphan and the captive﴾.

Others said: they were revealed concerning ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib, Fatimah, and their servant girl called Fiddah, and the story is as follows.

Al-Shaykh Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Ali al-Shaybani al-‘Adl informed us, reading it to him in Safar of the year three hundred and eighty-seven, saying: Ibn al-Sharqi informed us, saying: Mahbub ibn Hamid al-Nasri narrated to us, saying: Abu Muhammad ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Wahhab al-Khawwar, cousin of al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, narrated to us in the year two hundred and fifty-eight, and Rawh ibn ‘Ubadah asked him about this hadith, saying: al-Qayyim ibn Mihram narrated to us from Layth, from Mujahid, from Ibn ‘Abbas. And ‘Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Abu Muhammad Ahmad ibn ‘Abd Allah al-Muzani informed us, saying: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Suhayl ibn ‘Ali ibn Mihran al-Bahili narrated to us in Basra, saying: Abu Mas‘ud ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Fahd ibn Hilal narrated to us, saying: al-Ghanim ibn Yahya narrated to us, from Abu ‘Ali al-Qayri, from Muhammad ibn al-Sa’ir, from Abu Salih, from Ibn ‘Abbas. Abu al-Hasan ibn Mihran said: and Muhammad ibn Zakariyya al-Basri narrated to me, saying: Sa‘id ibn Waqid al-Muzani narrated to me, saying: al-Qasim ibn Bahram narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, from Ibn ‘Abbas, concerning God's saying ﴿They fulfil their vows, and fear a Day whose evil will be widespread﴾, that he said: al-Hasan and al-Husayn fell ill, and their grandfather Muhammad, the Messenger of God (ﷺ), visited them, with Abu Bakr and ‘Umar (may God be pleased with them both). The common Arabs also visited them, and they said: "O Abu al-Hasan, if you would vow a vow for your two sons. Every vow that is not fulfilled is nothing."

‘Ali (may God be pleased with him) said: "If my two sons recover from what they have, I will fast three days in thanks." Fatimah (may God be pleased with her) said: "If my two sons recover from what they have, I will fast three days for God in thanks." The two boys had not worn health, and there was nothing, little or much, with the family of Muhammad. So ‘Ali (may God be pleased with him) went to Shim‘un ibn Jaba al-Khaybari, who was a Jew, and borrowed from him three sa‘ of barley. In the narration of al-Muzani from Ibn Mihran al-Bahili: he went to a Jewish neighbour of his who worked wool, called Shim‘un ibn Jaba, and said: "Would you give me a fleece of wool, which the daughter of Muhammad (ﷺ) will spin for you in exchange for three sa‘ of barley?" He said: "Yes." So he gave it to him, and he brought the wool and the barley and informed Fatimah of this, and she accepted and obeyed.

They said: Fatimah (may God be pleased with her) stood up to one sa‘, ground it, and baked from it five loaves, one loaf for each of them. ‘Ali prayed the maghrib with the Prophet (ﷺ), then came to the house and placed the food before them. Suddenly a needy man came and stood at the door and said: "Peace be upon you, people of the house of Muhammad. A needy man from the needy Muslims: feed me, and God will feed you from the tables of Paradise." ‘Ali (may God be pleased with him) heard him and began to say:
"Fatimah, possessor of glory and certainty,
daughter of the best of all people,
do you not see the wretched needy man
who has stood at the door, moaning for him?
He complains to God and submits,
he complains to us, a hungry, sorrowful one.
Every person is held in pledge by his deeds,
and the doer of good will be made manifest.
Our promise is the garden of ‘Illiyyin,
which God has forbidden to the miser.
For the miser there is a humiliating station:
the fire will hurl him down into the prison.
His drink is boiling water and pus,
whoever does good will be made fat,
and will enter Paradise at any time."
Then Fatimah said:
"Your command is obeyed by me, cousin,
there is no baseness in me nor lowliness.
I was nourished on bread that has its craft,
I will feed him and not care for the hour.
I hope, when I satisfy the hungry one,
to join the righteous and the community,
and enter the eternal garden, and I have intercession."
He said: So they gave him the food, and they remained their day and night without tasting anything but plain water. When the second day came, Fatimah stood to another sa‘, ground it and baked it, and ‘Ali prayed with the Prophet (ﷺ). Then he came to the house and placed the food before them. Suddenly an orphan came and stood at the door and said: "Peace be upon you, people of the house of Muhammad. An orphan from the children of the emigrants; my father was martyred on the day of ‘Aqabah. Feed me, and God will feed you on the tables of Paradise." ‘Ali (may God be pleased with him) heard him and began to say:
"Fatimah, daughter of the noble master,
daughter of a prophet, not of the ignoble,
God has brought the orphan,
whoever shows mercy today will be shown mercy.
His promise is in the garden of bliss,
the eternity has been forbidden to the base.
Is it not that he will cross the straight path?
He who slips will fall into the fire of Hell."
Then Fatimah said:
"I feed him today and do not care,
and I prefer God over my children.
They have become hungry, and they are my cubs,
the youngest of them will be killed in battle.
At Karbala he will be killed by treachery,
for the killer there is woe and calamity.
Into the fire he will be hurled to the lowest depths,
and in his hands are fetters and chains,
his shackles increased over the shackles."
He said: So they gave him the food, and they remained two days and two nights without tasting anything but plain water. When it was the third day, Fatimah (may God be pleased with her) stood to the remaining sa‘, ground it and baked it, and ‘Ali prayed with the Prophet (ﷺ). Then he came to the house and placed the food before them. Suddenly a captive came and stood at the door and said: "Peace be upon you, people of the house of Muhammad. You take us captive [and bind us] and do not feed us. Feed me, for I am a captive of Muhammad. God will feed you on the tables of Paradise." ‘Ali heard him and began to say:
"Fatimah, daughter of the Prophet Ahmad,
daughter of a prophet, lord of the honoured,
this is a captive of the guided Prophet,
bound and shackled in his fetter,
he complains to us of hunger, it has stretched out.
Whoever feeds today will find it from tomorrow.
With the exalted, the one, the unifier,
what the sower sows, he will reap."
Then Fatimah said:
"Nothing remained of what had come except one sa‘.
My hand has gone with the forearm.
My sons, by God, are hungry.
O Lord, do not leave them lost.
Their father is one of good works,
who does kindness by innovation,
broad of forearms, long of reach,
and on my head is no veil,
except a veil woven of thongs."
He said: So they gave him the food, and they remained three days and nights without tasting anything but plain water. When it was the fourth day, and they had fulfilled their vow, ‘Ali (may God be pleased with him) took al-Hasan with his right hand and al-Husayn with his left, and came toward the Messenger of God (ﷺ), while they were trembling like chicks from the intensity of hunger. When the Prophet (ﷺ) saw them, he said: "O Abu al-Hasan, how grievous it is to me to see you in this state. Go to my daughter Fatimah." So they went to her, and she was in her prayer niche, her belly stuck to her back from intense hunger, and her eyes were sunken. When the Prophet (ﷺ) saw her, he said: "Woe, O God's help! The people of the house of Muhammad are dying of hunger." Then Gabriel (peace be upon him) descended and said: "O Muhammad, take it; God has blessed you in your household." He said: "What have we taken, O Gabriel?" [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/134; and Manaqib al-Khwarazmi: 270.]] Then he recited ﴿Has there come upon man a period of time﴾ up to his saying ﴿and not thanks﴾, to the end of the surah.

Qatadah ibn Mihran al-Bahili said in this hadith: The Prophet (ﷺ) leapt up until he entered upon Fatimah, and when he saw their state he bent over them weeping. Then he said: "You have been in this state for three days, as I see, and I was unaware of you." Then Gabriel (peace be upon him) descended with these verses: ﴿Indeed the righteous will drink from a cup whose mixture is camphor, a spring from which the servants of God will drink, making it gush forth in abundance.﴾ He said: it is a spring in the house of the Prophet (ﷺ) that gushes forth to the houses of the prophets (peace be upon them) and the believers.

﴿They fulfil their vows﴾, meaning ‘Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan, al-Husayn and their servant girl Fiddah. ﴿And they fear a Day whose evil will be widespread﴾. ﴿And they give food, despite their love for it﴾, meaning despite their desire for food, and preferring a needy person from the needy Muslims, an orphan from the orphans of the Muslims, and a captive from the captives of the polytheists. And when they fed them, they would say: ﴿We feed you only for the sake of God. We do not desire from you any reward or thanks. Indeed, we fear from our Lord a frowning Day, harsh﴾. He said: By God, they did not say this with their tongues, but they concealed it in their souls, so God, exalted is He, informed of their concealment: they say, ﴿We do not desire from you any reward or thanks﴾, so that they would not impose upon us by it, but we gave you for the sake of God and seeking His reward. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿So God protected them from the evil of that Day, and gave them radiance in their faces and joy in their hearts, and rewarded them for what they endured patiently: a garden in which to dwell, and silk to wear and to spread beneath them, reclining therein upon couches, they will see therein neither sun nor bitter cold.﴾

Ibn ‘Abbas said: While the people of Paradise are in Paradise, they will see a light like the light of the sun, and the gardens will shine with it. The people of Paradise will say: "O Ridwan!" He said: our Lord, mighty and majestic, says ﴿They will see therein neither sun nor bitter cold﴾. Ridwan will say to them: "This is neither sun nor moon, but this is Fatimah and ‘Ali laughing, laughing, and the gardens shine with the light of their laughter." And concerning them God, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿Has there come upon man a period of time﴾ to His saying: ﴿and your effort has been thankfully accepted.﴾

And I recited concerning him:
"I am the client of a young man
concerning whom ‘Has there come upon man' was revealed."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/138.]]

In light of this view, the surah is Madani. The scholars differed about when this surah was revealed. Mujahid and Qatadah said: all of it is Madani. Al-Hasan and Ikrimah said: one verse of it is Makki, namely His words, glory be to Him, ﴿So do not obey from among them any sinner or ungrateful one﴾, and the rest is Madani. Others said: all of it is Makki. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 76, verses 7–13 (part 1 of 2):

﴿They fulfil their vows﴾. Qatadah said: by what God, exalted is He, made obligatory upon them, such as prayer, zakat, hajj, umrah and other duties. Mujahid and ‘Ikrimah said: it means that when they vowed to obey God, they fulfilled it.

﴿And they fear a Day whose evil will be widespread﴾, i.e. extended and harsh. It is said: istatara al-sad'u fi al-zujajah (the crack spread through the glass) and istaṭāla, when it extended. From this is the saying of al-A‘sha:
"She departed, and she had left in the heart a crack
spreading far, despite her distance."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/128.]]

﴿And they give food, despite their love for it﴾. Ibn ‘Abbas said: despite its scarcity, their own need for it, and their desire for it. Al-Dari said: out of love for God. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: out of love for giving food.
﴿to the needy, the orphan and the captive﴾. The captive is the non-Muslim enemy seized by force, or the Muslim imprisoned with just cause. Qatadah said: after God commanded that captives be treated well, their captives at that time were from the polytheists, so your Muslim brother is more deserving that you feed him.
Mujahid, Sa‘id ibn Jubayr and ‘Ata said: it is the imprisoned person from among the People of the Qibla (Muslims).

Al-Hasan informed me, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Najiyah narrated to us, saying: ‘Abbad ibn Ahmad al-‘Arzami narrated to us, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to us, from his father, from ‘Amr ibn Qays, from ‘Atiyyah, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding ﴿And they give food, despite their love for it, to the needy﴾, that he said: "the poor"; ﴿and the orphan﴾, he said: "one who has no father"; ﴿and the captive﴾, he said: "the slave and the imprisoned."

Abu Hamzah al-Thumali said: the captive is the woman. The evidence for this interpretation is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Treat women well, for they are with you as captives." [[Sunan Ibn Majah: 1/594.]]

﴿We feed you only for the sake of God. We do not desire from you any reward or thanks.﴾ In it there are two readings: first, that shukūr is the plural of shukr, like fulūs as the plural of fals and kufūr as the plural of kufr; second, that it is a verbal noun, like fu‘ūl, dukhūl and khurūj.

Mujahid and Sa‘id ibn Jubayr said: they did not say this aloud, but God knew it from their hearts, so He praised them so that whoever desires it may be encouraged.

﴿Indeed, we fear from our Lord a Day that is frowning﴾, in which faces will frown because of its severity and abundance of hardships. He attributed the frowning to the Day, as one says "a fasting day" and "a sleeping night." Ibn ‘Abbas said: the disbeliever will frown on that day until sweat like tar flows from between his eyes. It was also said: the Day was described as frowning because of its hardship and terror, like a man with a grim and wretched face.

﴿Long and harsh﴾. ‘Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: "al-‘abus" means constriction, and "al-qamṭarīr" means long. Al-Kalbi said: "al-‘abus" is that which has no expansiveness, and "al-qamṭarīr" is severe. Qatadah, Mujahid and Muqatil said: "al-qamṭarīr" is that which contracts the faces, seizes life, and makes the space between the eyes contract because of its severity. Al-Akhfash said: al-qamṭarīr is the most intense and longest of days in affliction; it is said: yawm qamṭarīr and qamāṭir, when it is severe in its hardship. The poet said:
"They fled when the war's dust rose,
and the frowning, harsh day pressed upon them."
Al-Farra’ recited:
"Sons of our paternal uncle, do you remember our suffering
against you, when there was a harsh day?"
[[Al-Sihah: 2/797.]]
Al-Kisa’i said: iqmaṭarra al-qawm and izmaharra, iqmiṭrāran and izmihrāran, and it is zamharir and qamṭarir. A day is "muqmaṭir" when it is difficult and severe. Al-Hudhali said:
"The sons of war nursed us for them, a harsh milk,
so whoever of us meets that day flees."
[[The same source. In Taj al-‘Arus (3/507) it is narrated: "with it a harsh milk; whoever meets it meets a trained chief."]]

﴿So God protected them from the evil of that Day which they feared, and gave them radiance in their faces and joy in their hearts, and rewarded them for what they endured patiently﴾, in obedience to God and in abstaining from His disobedience. Al-Dahhak said: for poverty. Al-Qurtubi said: for fasting. ‘Ata said: for hunger.

Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab narrated from ‘Umar, who said: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was asked about patience, and he said: "Patience is of four kinds: first, patience at the first shock; second, patience in performing the obligations; third, patience in avoiding what God has forbidden; and fourth, patience in calamities." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/136.]]

﴿A garden and silk﴾. Al-Hasan said: He will admit them to Paradise and clothe them in silk.
﴿Reclining therein upon couches﴾, accusative as a circumstantial clause. ﴿Therein﴾, in Paradise. ﴿Upon couches﴾, the thrones inside canopied chambers; an arika is not called such unless both conditions are met. Al-Hasan said: this is the dialect of the people of Yemen, where a great man among them would make an arika, and it would be said: "the arika of so-and-so."

Muqatil said: al-ara’ik are thrones within canopied chambers, of pearls and rubies, interwoven with bars of gold and silver and various kinds of jewels.

﴿They will see therein neither sun nor bitter cold﴾, i.e. neither scorching heat nor freezing cold.
Qatadah said: God, exalted is He, knew that intense heat harms and intense cold harms, so God protected them from both harms together. Murrah al-Hamdani said: al-zamharir is the piercing cold. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: it is something like the heads of needles that descends from the sky in extreme cold. Ibn Mas‘ud said: it is a kind of punishment, which is intense cold.

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn ‘Imran al-Sawadi say: I heard Abu al-‘Abbas Ahmad ibn Yahya Tha‘lab, when he was asked about God's saying ﴿They will see therein neither sun nor bitter cold﴾, say: al-zamharir is the moon in the dialect of Tayy. Their poet said:
"A night whose darkness was thick,
I crossed it while the zamharir shone."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/138.]]
That is, the moon had not risen.

The scholars differed concerning the occasion of revelation of these verses. Muqatil said: they were revealed concerning a man from the Ansar who fed a needy person, an orphan and a captive in one day, and this was his story.

Ibn Fatjuwayh informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalaf ibn Hayyan narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn ‘Isa narrated to us, saying: ‘Ali ibn ‘Ali ibn Abi Hamzah al-Thumali narrated to us, saying: It reached us that a needy man came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, feed me." He said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, I have nothing with which to feed you, but I will seek." So he came to a man from the Ansar who was having his evening meal with his wife, and said to him: "I came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and asked him to feed me, and he said: 'I have nothing to feed you, but I will seek.'" The Ansari said to his wife: "What do you think?" She said: "Feed him and give him to drink." Then an orphan came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, feed me." He said: "I have nothing to feed you, but I will seek." So the orphan came to the Ansari who had been visited by the needy man and said: "Feed me." He said to his wife: "What do you think?" She said: "Feed him." So he fed him. Then a captive came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, feed me." He said: "By God, I have nothing to feed you, but I will seek." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/130.]] So the captive came to the Ansari and said: "Feed me." He said to his wife: "What do you think?" She said: "Feed him." All of this happened in a single hour, so God, exalted is He, revealed concerning what the Ansari did in feeding the needy, the orphan and the captive: ﴿And they give food, despite their love for it, to the needy, the orphan and the captive﴾.

Others said: they were revealed concerning ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib, Fatimah, and their servant girl called Fiddah, and the story is as follows.

Al-Shaykh Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Ali al-Shaybani al-‘Adl informed us, reading it to him in Safar of the year three hundred and eighty-seven, saying: Ibn al-Sharqi informed us, saying: Mahbub ibn Hamid al-Nasri narrated to us, saying: Abu Muhammad ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Wahhab al-Khawwar, cousin of al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, narrated to us in the year two hundred and fifty-eight, and Rawh ibn ‘Ubadah asked him about this hadith, saying: al-Qayyim ibn Mihram narrated to us from Layth, from Mujahid, from Ibn ‘Abbas. And ‘Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Abu Muhammad Ahmad ibn ‘Abd Allah al-Muzani informed us, saying: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Suhayl ibn ‘Ali ibn Mihran al-Bahili narrated to us in Basra, saying: Abu Mas‘ud ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Fahd ibn Hilal narrated to us, saying: al-Ghanim ibn Yahya narrated to us, from Abu ‘Ali al-Qayri, from Muhammad ibn al-Sa’ir, from Abu Salih, from Ibn ‘Abbas. Abu al-Hasan ibn Mihran said: and Muhammad ibn Zakariyya al-Basri narrated to me, saying: Sa‘id ibn Waqid al-Muzani narrated to me, saying: al-Qasim ibn Bahram narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, from Ibn ‘Abbas, concerning God's saying ﴿They fulfil their vows, and fear a Day whose evil will be widespread﴾, that he said: al-Hasan and al-Husayn fell ill, and their grandfather Muhammad, the Messenger of God (ﷺ), visited them, with Abu Bakr and ‘Umar (may God be pleased with them both). The common Arabs also visited them, and they said: "O Abu al-Hasan, if you would vow a vow for your two sons. Every vow that is not fulfilled is nothing."

‘Ali (may God be pleased with him) said: "If my two sons recover from what they have, I will fast three days in thanks." Fatimah (may God be pleased with her) said: "If my two sons recover from what they have, I will fast three days for God in thanks." The two boys had not worn health, and there was nothing, little or much, with the family of Muhammad. So ‘Ali (may God be pleased with him) went to Shim‘un ibn Jaba al-Khaybari, who was a Jew, and borrowed from him three sa‘ of barley. In the narration of al-Muzani from Ibn Mihran al-Bahili: he went to a Jewish neighbour of his who worked wool, called Shim‘un ibn Jaba, and said: "Would you give me a fleece of wool, which the daughter of Muhammad (ﷺ) will spin for you in exchange for three sa‘ of barley?" He said: "Yes." So he gave it to him, and he brought the wool and the barley and informed Fatimah of this, and she accepted and obeyed.

They said: Fatimah (may God be pleased with her) stood up to one sa‘, ground it, and baked from it five loaves, one loaf for each of them. ‘Ali prayed the maghrib with the Prophet (ﷺ), then came to the house and placed the food before them. Suddenly a needy man came and stood at the door and said: "Peace be upon you, people of the house of Muhammad. A needy man from the needy Muslims: feed me, and God will feed you from the tables of Paradise." ‘Ali (may God be pleased with him) heard him and began to say:
"Fatimah, possessor of glory and certainty,
daughter of the best of all people,
do you not see the wretched needy man
who has stood at the door, moaning for him?
He complains to God and submits,
he complains to us, a hungry, sorrowful one.
Every person is held in pledge by his deeds,
and the doer of good will be made manifest.
Our promise is the garden of ‘Illiyyin,
which God has forbidden to the miser.
For the miser there is a humiliating station:
the fire will hurl him down into the prison.
His drink is boiling water and pus,
whoever does good will be made fat,
and will enter Paradise at any time."
Then Fatimah said:
"Your command is obeyed by me, cousin,
there is no baseness in me nor lowliness.
I was nourished on bread that has its craft,
I will feed him and not care for the hour.
I hope, when I satisfy the hungry one,
to join the righteous and the community,
and enter the eternal garden, and I have intercession."
He said: So they gave him the food, and they remained their day and night without tasting anything but plain water. When the second day came, Fatimah stood to another sa‘, ground it and baked it, and ‘Ali prayed with the Prophet (ﷺ). Then he came to the house and placed the food before them. Suddenly an orphan came and stood at the door and said: "Peace be upon you, people of the house of Muhammad. An orphan from the children of the emigrants; my father was martyred on the day of ‘Aqabah. Feed me, and God will feed you on the tables of Paradise." ‘Ali (may God be pleased with him) heard him and began to say:
"Fatimah, daughter of the noble master,
daughter of a prophet, not of the ignoble,
God has brought the orphan,
whoever shows mercy today will be shown mercy.
His promise is in the garden of bliss,
the eternity has been forbidden to the base.
Is it not that he will cross the straight path?
He who slips will fall into the fire of Hell."
Then Fatimah said:
"I feed him today and do not care,
and I prefer God over my children.
They have become hungry, and they are my cubs,
the youngest of them will be killed in battle.
At Karbala he will be killed by treachery,
for the killer there is woe and calamity.
Into the fire he will be hurled to the lowest depths,
and in his hands are fetters and chains,
his shackles increased over the shackles."
He said: So they gave him the food, and they remained two days and two nights without tasting anything but plain water. When it was the third day, Fatimah (may God be pleased with her) stood to the remaining sa‘, ground it and baked it, and ‘Ali prayed with the Prophet (ﷺ). Then he came to the house and placed the food before them. Suddenly a captive came and stood at the door and said: "Peace be upon you, people of the house of Muhammad. You take us captive [and bind us] and do not feed us. Feed me, for I am a captive of Muhammad. God will feed you on the tables of Paradise." ‘Ali heard him and began to say:
"Fatimah, daughter of the Prophet Ahmad,
daughter of a prophet, lord of the honoured,
this is a captive of the guided Prophet,
bound and shackled in his fetter,
he complains to us of hunger, it has stretched out.
Whoever feeds today will find it from tomorrow.
With the exalted, the one, the unifier,
what the sower sows, he will reap."
Then Fatimah said:
"Nothing remained of what had come except one sa‘.
My hand has gone with the forearm.
My sons, by God, are hungry.
O Lord, do not leave them lost.
Their father is one of good works,
who does kindness by innovation,
broad of forearms, long of reach,
and on my head is no veil,
except a veil woven of thongs."
He said: So they gave him the food, and they remained three days and nights without tasting anything but plain water. When it was the fourth day, and they had fulfilled their vow, ‘Ali (may God be pleased with him) took al-Hasan with his right hand and al-Husayn with his left, and came toward the Messenger of God (ﷺ), while they were trembling like chicks from the intensity of hunger. When the Prophet (ﷺ) saw them, he said: "O Abu al-Hasan, how grievous it is to me to see you in this state. Go to my daughter Fatimah." So they went to her, and she was in her prayer niche, her belly stuck to her back from intense hunger, and her eyes were sunken. When the Prophet (ﷺ) saw her, he said: "Woe, O God's help! The people of the house of Muhammad are dying of hunger." Then Gabriel (peace be upon him) descended and said: "O Muhammad, take it; God has blessed you in your household." He said: "What have we taken, O Gabriel?" [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/134; and Manaqib al-Khwarazmi: 270.]] Then he recited ﴿Has there come upon man a period of time﴾ up to his saying ﴿and not thanks﴾, to the end of the surah.

Qatadah ibn Mihran al-Bahili said in this hadith: The Prophet (ﷺ) leapt up until he entered upon Fatimah, and when he saw their state he bent over them weeping. Then he said: "You have been in this state for three days, as I see, and I was unaware of you." Then Gabriel (peace be upon him) descended with these verses: ﴿Indeed the righteous will drink from a cup whose mixture is camphor, a spring from which the servants of God will drink, making it gush forth in abundance.﴾ He said: it is a spring in the house of the Prophet (ﷺ) that gushes forth to the houses of the prophets (peace be upon them) and the believers.

﴿They fulfil their vows﴾, meaning ‘Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan, al-Husayn and their servant girl Fiddah. ﴿And they fear a Day whose evil will be widespread﴾. ﴿And they give food, despite their love for it﴾, meaning despite their desire for food, and preferring a needy person from the needy Muslims, an orphan from the orphans of the Muslims, and a captive from the captives of the polytheists. And when they fed them, they would say: ﴿We feed you only for the sake of God. We do not desire from you any reward or thanks. Indeed, we fear from our Lord a frowning Day, harsh﴾. He said: By God, they did not say this with their tongues, but they concealed it in their souls, so God, exalted is He, informed of their concealment: they say, ﴿We do not desire from you any reward or thanks﴾, so that they would not impose upon us by it, but we gave you for the sake of God and seeking His reward. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿So God protected them from the evil of that Day, and gave them radiance in their faces and joy in their hearts, and rewarded them for what they endured patiently: a garden in which to dwell, and silk to wear and to spread beneath them, reclining therein upon couches, they will see therein neither sun nor bitter cold.﴾

Ibn ‘Abbas said: While the people of Paradise are in Paradise, they will see a light like the light of the sun, and the gardens will shine with it. The people of Paradise will say: "O Ridwan!" He said: our Lord, mighty and majestic, says ﴿They will see therein neither sun nor bitter cold﴾. Ridwan will say to them: "This is neither sun nor moon, but this is Fatimah and ‘Ali laughing, laughing, and the gardens shine with the light of their laughter." And concerning them God, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿Has there come upon man a period of time﴾ to His saying: ﴿and your effort has been thankfully accepted.﴾

And I recited concerning him:
"I am the client of a young man
concerning whom ‘Has there come upon man' was revealed."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/138.]]

In light of this view, the surah is Madani. The scholars differed about when this surah was revealed. Mujahid and Qatadah said: all of it is Madani. Al-Hasan and Ikrimah said: one verse of it is Makki, namely His words, glory be to Him, ﴿So do not obey from among them any sinner or ungrateful one﴾, and the rest is Madani. Others said: all of it is Makki. And Allah knows best.
